rationale: All three lenses ran against the spec and the Jira AC. Two blocking test gaps against the spec's testing matrix are emitted as CR-001 and CR-002. Deferred (2): Health check still uses a name-only existence check that can disagree with build (pre-existing, out of scope per spec). A delete that lands between drop_missing_context and get_tools can still raise (a narrow TOCTOU race that also existed before). Dismissed (11), each checked against the code: build_agent does not persist or cache the assistant (update/save only in create/update/publish endpoints). The lookup is equivalent to the removed get_deleted_context (same project filter and type mapping). Ruff F401/F821 are clean on the router. PROVIDER rows live in index_info. Workflow and tool-invoke virtual assistants never reach build_agent's filter (build_agent_for_workflow). The user-notice and all-deleted behaviour were chosen in the spec. The 12384 suites ran green in the 1610-test run.

findings.title: Real lookup and index_type→ContextType mapping have no test
findings.problem: Every new test patches _existing_context_keys, so the select on project_name/repo_name and Context.index_info_type_from_index_type are never exercised.
findings.impact: A wrong mapping (e.g. provider or code index_type prefix) would silently drop live datasources at every chat without any test failing.
findings.recommendation: Add a test that patches Session so session.exec(...).all() returns rows like ('kb', 'knowledge_base...'), ('repo', '<code type>'), ('prov', '<provider type>') and asserts the returned keys carry KNOWLEDGE_BASE/CODE/PROVIDER.

findings.title: KB-missing case from the spec matrix is not covered
findings.problem: The spec lists KB / CODE / PROVIDER missing; only CODE and PROVIDER deletions are tested.
findings.impact: The most common datasource type is not pinned by a test.
findings.recommendation: Add a case where a KNOWLEDGE_BASE context is missing while a CODE context exists, asserting the KB entry is dropped and CODE kept.
